key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 non-routed AI caught the structural infeasibility (20×33 = 660 > 480) and predicted gaming but then treated the HQ mandate as fixed and deepened monitoring — feeding the KPI-illusion loop instead of changing loop structure; it missed the support-bottleneck amplifier, gave no markers with timing, and its own REVIEW flagged the error it could not correct. The v6 routed run closed all three gaps as m086 completion-contract outputs (5 signed loops incl. R1 comp-attrition, B3 support-bottleneck, R2 KPI-illusion; policy resistance located in the time stock as a conservation law; a falsifiable observable attached to EVERY loop with Q2-Q4 timing), with m023 opportunity-cost pricing (keep-mandate options forfeit the outcome contract), m070 evidence-graded SWOT (drops the unbacked 'quota forces phone time' claim), m003 ranked failure categories of the redesign itself, and m088 pre-commitment framing of reset triggers; residual shared gap: the human's pure trace remains marginally more efficient than the gate machinery (human 5 vs AI 4.5 efficiency; overall 4.9/4.9, J1 second-judge flag noted).
learning_signal: When a policy is structurally infeasible, the policy is a decision variable, not a constraint — and the m086 pass must prove resistance structurally: (1) state the mechanism as a stock-level conservation law (time/effort-budget arithmetic: 660 > 480, and 500 > 480 at zero admin); (2) map every loop SIGNED with a FALSIFIABLE OBSERVABLE attached per loop (a marker that distinguishes that loop from the others — timestamp clustering for gaming, median talk time for time-compression, attrition rate for comp-attrition, backlog for the bottleneck, paper-vs-real divergence for KPI-illusion); (3) generate at least one alternative that changes loop structure (remove the quota / rewire comp / add capacity) checked against the binding arithmetic, never just intensifying enforcement; (4) pre-commit reset triggers — rollback-by-design thresholds that bind the org's future self, treating the policy change as a Ulysses contract so rollback happens by design, not post-mortem.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m023+m070 dual-route with m088 context and the m003 inversion gate on estimate/guarantee/predict + organization-policy signatures (router confident=no); make per-loop falsifiable observables and reset-trigger pre-commitments standing m086 contract items; add the m070 evidence-graded-SWOT discipline (drop claims the historical record contradicts) as a checklist rule; retain the m003 failure-categories pass applied to the RECOMMENDED redesign, not just to the status quo.

key_gap: vs baseline: both sides correctly refused the reductionist trap (v5 AI and human both signed the patch, deferred the council, gated residual levers — the human's margin was the aftermath pass: the AI mentioned freed capacity in one clause, never quantified it (8 × 90% ≈ 7.2 agent-equivalents; 45% cut frees ≈ 3.2), named no make-work or morale/hoarding loop, and had no redeployment ladder; its uncertainty handling was informal. The v6 routed run closed the aftermath gap as the m086 estimator-vs-structure output (data-first ordering: no loop map over the measured 45%; aftermath loops with falsifiable observables — new-process count and disposition-time creep; redeployment: OT → backlog → proactive) and exceeded both baselines on uncertainty: m006 provenance audit (3 likelihood scenarios 0.70/0.85/0.95 → posterior range 45 ± 10% removal → decision-threshold flip demonstrated) and m019's quantified delay vector (4 months × 540/wk ≈ 8,640 tickets ≈ 2,160 agent-hours left running); tempo mode (c:deadline) kept efficiency high while committing at DO; overall 4.7 human vs 4.9 AI, J1 second-judge flag noted.
learning_signal: Estimator-vs-structure ordering is the reductionism guard for org analysis: (1) never draw a loop map over a measured cause — a loop 'explaining' measured volume via org dynamics is fabrication; the direct measured lever executes first, and loop analysis applies only to the change's aftermath and the unmeasured residual; (2) a mandatory aftermath pass after ANY change: quantify the capacity/stock released by arithmetic, name at least two signed response loops (make-work under freed capacity, morale/utilization cliff with hoarding and scope-expansion), attach a falsifiable observable to each, and specify a redeployment ladder — selecting a lever is not the end of the task; (3) under unmeasured context, run the provenance audit with ≥ 3 likelihood scenarios, a posterior range, and a demonstrated decision-threshold flip before any org-dynamics claim is licensed; (4) price the delay vector of any program against the measured lever it postpones (council cost = 8,640 tickets left running).
suggested_improvement: Keep the m019+m018+m026 single-route with the m006 provenance gate on deadline+unmeasured signatures (router confident=yes); install the aftermath pass (capacity arithmetic + named response loops with falsifiable observables + redeployment ladder) as a standing m086/m011 contract item on ALL change interventions, not just this case; add delay-vector quantification (program cost expressed in units of the lever it postpones) as a mandatory m019 packet line; retain tempo mode for c:deadline — commit at DO without silencing the scheduled post-fix re-measure (the day-14 gate that decides the residual levers).
